text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- High Court supports judge Javier Gomez de Liano's bid to declassify military intelligence papers linked to 1980s "dirty war" against Basque separatists.
- Five nuclear powers sign nuclear test ban treaty.
- Director of paramilitary Civil Guard says former Socialist government left budget gap of 41 billion pesetas.
- Environment Minister Isabel Tocino clashes with Defence Minister Eduardo Serra over military shooting range in Anchuras.
EL MUNDO
- High Court reminds government that right to life overrules secrecy.
- Monica Ridruejo, director of state television, asks government for 274 billion pesetas for 1997.
DIARIO 16
- High Court corners government on "dirty war".
- Spanish organisation asks for one million pesetas for the adoption of each Russian child.
ABC
- Government seals pact over budget with Catalan nationalist Convergence and Unity (CiU) coalition and agrees on pensions with unions.
- More than 50 countries sign nuclear test ban treaty in United Nations.
CINCO DIAS
- Bread today, taxes tomorrow: government and unions to announce agreement on pensions.
- 27 hypermarkets on Competition Tribunal's waiting list for permission to open.
- Lawyers suspended by Cajamadrid reinstated.
EXPANSION
- Savings banks of Orense, Pontevedra and Vigo studying merger.
- Sugar refiner Azucarera and Ebro moving towards integration.
- Seat chairman Joan Llorens says has fulfilled his duties and will remain linked to Seat after stepping down.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Employment Minister Javier Arenas gives in to unions and avoids reforming pensions.
- Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo maintains key money market rate at 7.25 percent, leaving rate cut hopes open.
- Bourse proposes reducing hours for trading low liquidity shares.
- Construction group Huarte to fire 500 workers as part of second adjustment plan.
- Industry Minister Josep Pique says public firms will cost one trillion pesetas in 1997.
